title: Common-Gate Stage
intro: In the common-gate (CG) stage the signal enters at the source and exits at the drain, with the gate held at a DC bias.

blocks.source:
Av = gm*RD   (non-inverting; with RS: gm*RD / (1 + gm*RS))
Rin = 1/gm   (higher with a load: about 1/gm + RD/(gm*ro) )
Rout = RD || [ro*(1 + gm*RS) + RS]

items: The input resistance 1/gm is low, so a CG stage is a good current buffer: it loads a current source with a small impedance and passes the current to RD.
Gain is the same size as the CS gain, but the signal does not invert.
Body effect actually helps: gm is replaced by gm + gmb in the gain expression, increasing it by a factor (1 + eta).
CG is the top half of the cascode and is also used for matching a source impedance, as in an RF low-noise amplifier.

blocks.title: Input resistance and gain
blocks.text: gm = 2 mS, gmb = 0, RD = 5 kohm, source driven by a signal source of resistance RS = 500 ohm. Find the voltage gain Vout/Vin (including RS as a divider) and the input resistance.
solution: Rin = 1/gm = 500 ohm. The source resistance RS = 500 ohm and Rin form a divider with ratio Rin/(Rin+RS) = 0.5.
The gain from the stage input to output is gm*RD = 10, so the gain from the source is 0.5 * 10 = 5. The same answer comes from gm*RD/(1 + gm*RS) = 10/2 = 5.
